Chapter 8: Cultivating Self-Compassion and Letting Go of Perfectionism.
As you keep moving forward, have you noticed that little voice of self-criticism popping up now and then? You’re not alone—it happens to all of us, especially when perfectionism sneaks in.
Let’s talk about why it matters to treat yourself with the same kindness and understanding you’d offer a good friend. That’s what self-compassion is all about.
Perfectionism usually comes from a fear of falling short or that never-ending need for approval. Maybe you’ve felt it too—when you hesitate to start something because it might not be perfect, or you push yourself so hard you end up feeling burned out and never quite “enough.”
Here’s something to pay attention to: Mistakes and imperfections aren’t signs of failure—they’re just part of how we grow. Think about a child learning to walk. Every time they stumble, we cheer them on, right? We don’t judge them harshly. Adults deserve that same gentle encouragement and understanding.
So, what can you do differently?
First, start noticing when your inner critic speaks up. When you catch those harsh thoughts, try swapping them out for supportive, encouraging words. If you wouldn’t say it to a friend, don’t say it to yourself.
Set goals that are realistic—shoot for “good enough” rather than chasing perfection every time. And don’t forget to celebrate the small wins along the way. Give yourself credit for the effort you put in, not just the end results.
Another part of self-compassion is learning to forgive yourself for past mistakes. We all have moments we wish we could redo, but hanging onto regret or shame just drains your energy. When you accept your imperfections and learn from setbacks, it gets easier to move forward without feeling weighed down.
Here’s a simple practice you might try: Take some time to reflect on challenges you’ve faced. What lessons did you take away from them? Practice letting go of those unrealistic expectations, and give yourself the same patience you’d offer someone you love.
By choosing self-compassion, you create a kinder, more supportive environment inside yourself. That makes it so much easier to push through tough times and keep your momentum going.
